title: From Language to Navigation Goals: A Vision-Language Approach for Semantic Navigation of Mobile Robots Using RGB-D Perception
abstract: arXiv:2607.13624v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Natural language interaction provides an intuitive way for non-expert users to communicate with robotic platforms. However, transforming user requests into executable navigation actions remains a challenging task, requiring the integration of language understanding, environment perception, and autonomous navigation. This work presents a language-driven navigation framework that enables mobile robots to interpret user requests in natural language to move the robot to a destination and autonomously navigate towards it.   The framework is composed of modular ROS 2 components that cooperate to transform natural language instructions into navigation actions. Given a natural language request referring to a target in the environment (e.g., "go to the mail box"), the system identifies the referenced object, estimates its position using RGB-D data, and generates a navigation goal, which is then executed through the ROS 2 Nav2 navigation

translated_title: 从语言到导航目标：基于RGB-D感知的移动机器人语义导航的视觉-语言方法
translated_abstract: 自然语言交互为非专业用户提供了一种与机器人平台进行直观交流的方式。然而，将用户请求转化为可执行的导航动作仍然是一项具有挑战性的任务，需要整合语言理解、环境感知和自主导航。本工作提出了一个语言驱动的导航框架，使移动机器人能够理解用户以自然语言表达的移动到目的地的请求，并自主导航到达该目的地。该框架由模块化的ROS 2组件构成，这些组件协同工作，将自然语言指令转化为导航动作。给定一个引用环境中目标的自然语言请求（例如“去邮箱”），系统会识别所引用的物体，利用RGB-D数据估计其位置，并生成导航目标，随后通过ROS 2 Nav2导航系统执行该目标。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个由模块化ROS 2组件构成的语言驱动导航框架，利用RGB-D感知识别自然语言指令中目标物体的位置，使移动机器人能够将非专业用户的自然语言请求直接转化为可执行的自主导航目标。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a language-driven navigation framework composed of modular ROS 2 components that uses RGB-D perception to localize target objects referenced in natural language commands, enabling mobile robots to translate non-expert users' natural language requests directly into executable autonomous navigation goals.
